candidates.title: ScaleTrains HO scale EMD SD40-2 diesel locomotive
candidates.excerpt: Model Railroader Senior Editor Cody Grivno takes the throttle to evaluate the ScaleTrains HO scale (1:87.1) EMD SD40-2 diesel locomotive in this latest product review video! Our review model depicts Burlington Northern Santa Fe No. 8010, an EMD 3,000hp workhorse decorated in the eye-catching Heritage 1 paint scheme. The locomotive features prototypical details such as a nose-mounted headlight, semi-scale knuckle couplers, wire grab irons, see-through radiator fan grilles, and HTC truck sideframes with painted wheel faces. Equipped with an ESU LokSound V5 decoder and dual cube-type speakers, the model delivers realistic sounds, including engine startup (F8), horn (F2), and sanding valves (F18). Direct-current versions retail for $219.99, while DCC sound-equipped models sell for $329.99. Watch Cody using the unit to switch along the Milwaukee, Racine & Troy! Trains.com Product Review videos showcase the latest new items from manufacturers of products in Z, N, HO, S, O, and large scales.

However, the operating environment remained challenging for terminals in the UAE, where geopolitical disruptions continued to affect cargo flows. candidates.title: US container imports hit all-time high in October, Descartes reports
candidates.excerpt: US container imports reached an all-time monthly high in October 2026, supported by stronger shipments from China and increased activity at East and Gulf Coast ports, according to Descartes Systems Group. The latest Global Shipping Report shows that US maritime container imports reached 2,674,808 TEUs in October. This represents a 5% increase from September and a 16% rise compared with October 2025. The total exceeded the previous monthly record of 2,622,465 TEUs, set in May 2022, by 52,343 TEUs. During the first ten months of 2026, US container imports increased by 2.3% compared with the same period last year. This marked the second consecutive month in which cumulative volumes remained above their 2025 levels. China imports strengthen as East and Gulf Coast ports gain Imports from China rose for the fourth consecutive month, reaching 987,805 TEUs in October. candidates.title: RCL posts higher Q3 profit and orders 12 containerships
candidates.excerpt: Regional Container Lines (RCL) reported a sharp increase in third-quarter profit as higher freight rates supported earnings despite lower container volumes. The Thailand-based shipping company recorded a net profit of THB 3.26 billion for the three months ended 30 September 2026. This represents a 64.7% increase from THB 1.98 billion in the previous quarter. Freight income rose by THB 1.05 billion, or 10.4%, compared with the second quarter. Meanwhile, freight and operating costs declined by 2.4%, supporting the improvement in profitability. However, total container liftings fell by 4.1% during the quarter. RCL attributed the stronger earnings partly to higher freight rates caused by congestion at major ports and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The company’s average freight rate increased from US$552 per TEU in the second quarter to US$624 per TEU in the third quarter. candidates.excerpt: Evergreen resumes Suez Canal transits after nearly 3-year hiatus Evergreen resumed its shipping services across the Suez Canal following a nearly three-year hiatus amid the Red Sea crisis, Osama Rabie, Chairman of the Suez Canal Authority (SCA), announced. The giant container ship Ever Eon, part of the Evergreen fleet, made its first transit through the canal on Sunday, November 8, as part of the northbound convoy, sailing from the Netherlands to Singapore. The vessel is 369 meters long and 53.6 meters wide, with a gross tonnage of 185,000 tons and a carrying capacity of up to 16,556 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs). Rabie emphasized that this step is a positive indicator that global trade between the East and the West is moving back toward a sustainable path. candidates.title: LR: Partnering the right yard to the right project
candidates.excerpt: LR: Partnering the right yard to the right project For shipowners planning their next generation of vessels, the newbuilding decision has rarely carried more strategic weight. A new construction boom, driven by demand for containerships and gas carriers, is coinciding with an ageing global fleet and a rapidly evolving regulatory and technology landscape. The ships ordered today will remain in service for decades, operating through the energy transition and, in many cases, into a net-zero emissions supply chain by 2050. That reality is changing how owners approach new construction. Yard availability, delivery schedules and commercial terms remain critical, but they are no longer enough on their own. Future-fuel capability and emissions performance are now central to the specification process, while digital integration, build quality, regulatory readiness and long-term asset value will determine how vessels perform throughout their operating lives. candidates.title: NTSB releases preliminary report on UP derailment in Kansas
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Damage was estimated at $2.4 million after 37 cars of a Union Pacific train derailed near Greensburg, Kan., on Oct. 15, according to a preliminary report from the National Transportation Safety Board. The train was westbound on UP’s Pratt Subdivision with three head-end locomotives, two midtrain distributed power units, and 171 loaded intermodal cars and auto racks when it derailed about 8:25 a.m. There were no injuries and no hazardous materials were released. Prior to the derailment, the train had been running at about 56 mph when it was stopped by a penalty brake application. After confirming that communication was intact with the DPUs and end-of-train device, and restoring brake pipe pressure, the engineer resumed the trip, but the train was stopped shortly thereafter by an emergency brake application, at which time the conductor observed the derailed cars. candidates.title: Switch installation celebrated at Pullman historic park
candidates.excerpt: CHICAGO — Visitors to the 19th-century Pullman factory complex on Chicago’s South Side frequently ask, “Where are the railcars?” The first step in eliminating that question took place when Norfolk Southern recently reinstalled a switch on an industrial lead two blocks east of the site that was once the conduit in and out of the sprawling plant. Next, a track will be relaid from there along the north side of 111th Street, now a grassy parkway, to a planned building to display vintage Pullman equipment. Norfolk Southern is contributing $250,000 to the venture. On Monday, Nov. 9, Friends of the Pullman National Historical Park staged a “Setting the Spikes” event. Local dignitaries were invited to don protective gear before bringing sledgehammers down on a track slab NS placed in a parking lot nowhere near where the real track will be constructed. candidates.title: Memphis-area town asks STB to require UP to keep NS intermodal terminal open
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — The town of Rossville, Tenn., has asked the Surface Transportation Board to require Union Pacific to keep Norfolk Southern’s Memphis-area intermodal terminal open for at least five years after the merger. The UP-NS operating plan assumes UP will close the Rossville terminal in favor of its terminal across the Mississippi River in Marion, Ark. NS handles about 500 daily lifts at Rossville, a $125.6 million terminal that opened in 2012 with construction partly funded through a $52.5 million federal grant. Shifting Rossville’s containers to Marion would increase Marion truck traffic by 57% and force Memphis-area containers to cross the Mississippi by rail and return by truck, adding bridge traffic and drayage expense, the town argues in a filing with the STB. candidates.title: AAR Reports Weekly Rail Traffic for the Week Ending October 31, 2026
candidates.excerpt: The Association of American Railroads (AAR) reported U.S. rail traffic for the week ending October 31, 2026. For this week, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 514,080 carloads and intermodal units, up 3.5 percent compared with the same week last year. Total carloads for the week ending October 31 were 233,816 carloads, up 3.0 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 280,264 containers and trailers, up 3.9 percent compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals, up 3,883 carloads, to 25,059; chemicals, up 2,542 carloads, to 34,523; and motor vehicles and parts, up 1,351 carloads, to 16,268. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were grain, down 2,092 carloads, to 23,078; miscellaneous carloads, down 1,162 carloads, to 8,369; and coal, down 224 carloads, to 55,042.
